highlights: More than one million Koreans celebrated the first anniversary of liberation in Seoul on 15 August, marked by the ceremonial return of the 1910 Annexation Treaty and nine historic royal seals.

Lt. Gen. John R. Hodge and Soviet Col. Gen. I. M. Chistiakov exchanged published letters over the Joint Commission deadlock, Hodge urging reconvening and rejecting ideological restrictions on Korean democratic participation.

General Hodge directed the transfer of operational civil administration to Korean officials, leaving American personnel largely in advisory roles; Ordinance No. 104 created the Department of Public Works.
Ordinance No. 103 established a seven-member Property Claims Commission with final authority to settle disputed titles to Japanese property.
Ordinance No. 102 founded Seoul National University, merging nine existing colleges and institutes under a unified Board of Regents.
National Food Regulation No. 2 set local quotas and administrative procedures for the 1946-1947 rice collection program, while post-flood crop rehabilitation continued.
A major cholera epidemic produced 10,648 cases and 6,894 deaths, with nearly ten million vaccine units distributed and fishery bans imposed.
An appendix reviews the first year of military government, 7 September 1945 to 31 August 1946, including education reaching 1.7 million students with Korean textbooks.

summary: This eleventh monthly summation covers United States Army Military Government activities in South Korea during August 1946, marking the first anniversary of liberation from Japanese colonial rule. Significant political events include the mass celebration of Liberation Day on 15 August, the ceremonial return of the 1910 Annexation Treaty and nine historic Korean royal seals, and published correspondence between Lieutenant General John R. Hodge and Soviet Colonel General I. M. Chistiakov regarding deadlock in the Joint Commission. The administration established the Department of Public Works (Ordinance 104) and the Property Claims Commission (Ordinance 103), while General Hodge directed the transfer of operational administration to Korean personnel. Economic reporting focuses on post-flood agricultural recovery, National Food Regulation No. 2 instituting the 1946-1947 rice collection system, and the extensive holdings of the New Korea Company. Social affairs highlight containment of a severe cholera epidemic that caused nearly 7,000 deaths, the founding of Seoul National University (Ordinance 102), and mass repatriation. A special one-year appendix comprehensively reviews occupation policies since September 1945. For historians, the issue provides critical primary documentation on Korean civil administration, political factionalism, educational reform, and public health management.
